column2: Peter Bressan, London (alto recorder 'd', Frans Bruggen collection, Amsterdam; drawing No. X by Fred Morgan, Zen-On 1981); numbers as tabulated by Jan Bouterse
baroque alto recorder in F, boxwood with ivory rings, in three joints (head, middle joint, foot), seven finger holes and a thumb hole
about 1700 (Bressan worked in London from 1688); tables 2009 to 2010
baroque recorder: curved windway, block, window and labium in the head; thumb hole and seven finger holes (holes 6 and 7 double on some altos)
Frans Bruggen collection, Amsterdam (the instrument is in fine condition and was played on a Handel sonatas recording)
pitch measurements made at 15 to 27 C in several rooms; the instrument was measured in its present, shrunken and slightly oval state

one real alto recorder with published bore, hole and window geometry; the windway height is not published for it; no recording of it is in the library and no licensed reference exists yet (bead pexfp.219), so renders are listened to, not graded

hole-00 is the thumb hole (back of the middle joint); hole-01 to hole-06 are the front holes from the head down; hole-07 is on the foot; positions are measured from the upper shoulder of the middle joint along the bore, except where a feature says otherwise
plays at about a1 = 409 Hz (Bouterse: alto d- is about 40 cents below a1 = 415 Hz at 20 C)
